uncertainty: Frequency and handling time of transport questions at target hotels.
Who controls a hotel budget and whether €25 per month is acceptable.
Coverage, freshness and conflict handling across relevant official notices.
Actual checker design and human review workload.
Supplier costs beyond payment processing and comparative manual preparation cost.
dissent: A narrowly scoped, manually checked card service could be useful before extensive automation; modest demand might justify further research even without demonstrated willingness to pay.
Ten questions per receptionist can reveal obvious failures but cannot establish operational reliability or broad hotel demand.

say: Do not target NGOs merely because you can find an audience. The NGO seminar receipt establishes an invitation to organisers, not repeated tableware-sourcing difficulty. Your proposed three quote requests would show prospective interest, not recurrence or NGO-specific need. Run one comparative discovery-and-quote test within the proposed €20 cap: recruit five NGO and five non-NGO organisers through permitted channels, using the same eligibility rule of at least two events organised in the past year. uncertainty: Whether NGO organisers repeatedly encounter consequential sourcing failures, rather than one-off inconvenience.
Whether those failures are more concentrated among NGOs than comparable non-NGO organisers.
Whether organisers with documented recurring difficulty would pursue a dated quote with the proposed €3 fee disclosed.
